preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is a positive integer.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(N, int) and isinstance(K, int) and 1 <= K <= N <= 200000 for N, K in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, N and K are integers satisfying 1 <= K <= N <= 2*10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(all(isinstance(x, int) and 0 <= x <= 10**9 for x in A) for A in all_A_lists)
preconditions.description: All node values A_i are integers between 0 and 10^9 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == N - 1 and all(1 <= u <= N and 1 <= v <= N and u != v for u, v in edges) for edges, N in zip(all_edges_lists, all_N_list))
preconditions.description: Each test case provides exactly N-1 edges connecting distinct nodes within the range [1, N], forming a tree.
The sum of N over all test cases does not exceed 2*10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(int(line), int) and int(line) >= 0 for line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is a non-negative integer representing the maximum possible bitwise AND of the XOR sums of the K trees.

postconditions.expression: all(max_possible_and(N, K, A, edges) == int(stdout_lines[i]) for i, (N, K, A, edges) in enumerate(zip(all_N_list, all_K_list, all_A_lists, all_edges_lists)))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output value equals the maximum possible value of the bitwise AND of the XOR sums of K disjoint trees formed by partitioning the original tree nodes, where max_possible_and computes this optimal value based on the input tree structure and node values.
